name: semantic-release

extends.description: List of modules or file paths containing a shareable configuration. If multiple shareable configurations are set, they will be imported in the order defined with each configuration option taking precedence over the options defined in a previous shareable configuration

branches.description: The branches on which releases should happen.

tagFormat.description: The Git tag format used by semantic-release to identify releases. The tag name is generated with Lodash template and will be compiled with the version variable.

plugins.description: Define the list of plugins to use. Plugins will run in series, in the order defined

dryRun.description: The objective of the dry-run mode is to get a preview of the pending release. Dry-run mode skips the following steps: prepare, publish, success and fail. In addition to this it prints the next version and release notes to the console

ci.description: Set to false to skip Continuous Integration environment verifications. This allows for making releases from a local machine

description:
We’re using a shared configuration that extends both the standard @semantic-release/npm-config package and a custom file located at ./release-config.js. Our release workflow will run on the main branch, as well as on a few special branches: a beta branch that publishes prereleases on the “beta” channel, an rc branch that uses “rc” as its prerelease identifier, and a 1.x branch that is limited to versions in the range >=1.0.0 < 2.0.0. The source code lives at https://github.com/example/project.git, and tags will be created using the pattern release-${version}.

The plugin stack is the usual set, starting with @semantic-release/commit-analyzer, followed by @semantic-release/release-notes-generator configured to use the “conventionalcommits” preset, then @semantic-release/npm, and finally @semantic-release/github which is set up to attach any files matching dist/*.tgz as “Distribution” assets. The process will run in normal mode (dry‑run is disabled) and will perform the usual CI environment checks (ci is enabled).
